stem: Why is a spacer generally recommended on a paediatric asthma action plan?

options.text: It improves delivery of the medication to the lungs in children
It is only needed when using a dry powder inhaler
It is required to measure peak flow accurately
It reduces the prescribed dose needed for effect
It replaces the need for a reliever inhaler

explanation: A spacer improves delivery of inhaled medication to the lungs in children by helping the medicine get past the throat and into the lower airways.
rationale: Young children often have difficulty coordinating actuation and inhalation with a puffer, so a spacer improves effective drug delivery.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because spacers help overcome coordination problems and improve the amount of medication reaching the lower airways.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because spacers are used with pressurised metered-dose inhalers, not dry powder inhalers.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because peak flow measurement is done with a peak flow meter, not a spacer.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a spacer improves delivery efficiency but does not reduce the prescribed dose.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a spacer assists inhaler delivery but does not replace the reliever medication.

source.hint: Think about the mechanical challenges young children face when trying to coordinate their breathing with a puffer.
